ADDED 2026-09-19 (mid-run, measured on James's machine): list FIRST among the wrapper's correctness items - the MCP watcher (repo_graph/watcher.py `_Handler.on_any_event`) triggers a rebuild on EVERY watchdog event, and watchdog 6.0 on Linux emits read-only `opened` / `closed_no_write` events (6 s sample on glia: opened 9161, closed_no_write 9160, modified 2). A rebuild opens every source file, so each rebuild schedules the next: an endless loop that wrote ~1.2 TB in a day (parse_cache.bin rewritten every ~1.4 s) with nobody editing. Fix in the wrapper: rebuild only on event_type created / modified / moved / deleted / closed. This is separate from the `.glia/graph` SKIP_DIRS change LC.9 already hands off (write events from the new layout dir); the handoff needs both. glia's half (write the parse cache only when it changed) is LC.11.

HANDOFF FROM LC.11 (w21): LG.5a (repo-graph watcher): glia no longer rewrites parse_cache.bin on a no-change rebuild. Once the 0.5.0 wheel is in, the watcher can verify this with `grep '^\[incremental\] unchanged'` on its stderr. The rebuild itself (walk + parse-cache load + resolve) still runs on every event until the watcher stops triggering on read-only inotify events, so both fixes are needed.

An id present in two language graphs of one repo (TS + Dart calling the same canonical path) therefore emits duplicate identical HTTP_CALLS edges, and the `[http] endpoints/paired` counters count entries, not nodes. The fix is a seen-set keyed on NodeId as in grpc.rs pair_servers, taking the strongest entry confidence and the union of ENDPOINT_HIT cells for host narrowing.
